registry_info.name: vectors_demos
registry_info.description: Vector concept demonstration artifacts — applied physics demos showing vectors in action: force addition, work/energy, torque, reflection, and targeting.
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: Vector algebra, dot product (work, projection), cross product (torque, normals), force superposition, targeting and aiming algorithms

wedge_slide.name: Wedge Slide (inclined-plane free body)
wedge_slide.description: The inclined-plane free-body problem made playable - a primitive on a wedge, the force-decomposition toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A ToyConsole: the INCLINE slider sets the angle θ; the 3D demo shows the block on the slope with its force vectors (weight mg, normal N, friction f, and the net down-slope force); and the MONITOR draws the flat 2D free-body section - the textbook triangle with mg resolved into mg sinθ (down the slope) and mg cosθ (into it), N, friction, and the θ arc, auto-fit to the screen. Tilt past tan θ = μ and it goes from STATIC to SLIDING. mu is the (fixed) friction coefficient.

parameters.incline: 0..1 incline angle θ (12° to 55°) - past tan θ = μ the block slides (default 0.5)

dna.default: workings=trace - trace is the fall-through arm of the match and runs no code at all, and the whole match sits AFTER _settle(rig, 2.8), so the legacy fit, scale and placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. The only edit above that line binds five nodes to locals that were previously passed straight into add_child, plus an identity Node3D named ThetaArc holding the eleven arc spheres so the axis can reach the whole arc in one call; pickable_prop._subtree_aabb recurses into Node3D children and does NOT apply their transform, and this holder is never moved, so the settled box is bit-identical to the one that ships. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, MindMap_VectorForces, Vectors_Act4a_KineticForces) carry the bare token `force_mower` or `force_mower:0:0` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists - and when it IS reached, an unrecognised word is ignored rather than assigned, so a typo falls back to the shipped picture instead of blanking the diagram.
dna.was: no axis. Seven exports - a seed, a 0..1 push_angle and five colours - could move or recolour ONE fixed diagram, and the runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. What the machine draws OF the work was welded into _build and drawn always, in the same order: F down the handle, the horizontal F cos theta, the dashed green waste, the theta arc, the long purple displacement and a billboard readout. A map could set how STEEP the push was and what COLOUR it was, never what the object claimed the product W = F d cos theta is made of.
dna.shared_with: transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded on this bench by dot_aligner, vector_add, vector_sub, projection_shadow, launch_arc, torque_crank, bounce_well and length_lantern. W = F.d is the dot product doing manual labour - the same product those benches take apart - so it takes their word rather than inventing a second vocabulary for one question. DERIVED from the @export_enum in force_mower.gd, not transcribed.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. Each value names something this object genuinely has, which is the test for borrowing a word. OUTCOME is where this member departs from its family and earns the word rather than renting it: every sibling answers `outcome` with a length left lying on a rail, and this one answers with a change in the world. All five vectors and the readout leave the render layers and what remains is a machine standing on grass with a strip cut out of it - the work done, stated as mown ground. OPERANDS fixes something the shipped picture never said out loud: F is drawn at the grip and d is drawn down at ankle height, so the two factors of the product never meet and the diagram never claims they are two vectors at an angle. Here d is redrawn leaving the grip beside F, theta is swept between them at double the shipped radius, and a right-angle gnomon is planted where F drops onto the line of d; the DERIVED quantities go dark, because F cos theta and the wasted F sin theta are answers and not ingredients. EXPRESSION stands a plate above the machine writing W = F . d . cos theta with the DRAWN numbers substituted - F_MAG and D_MAG, the lengths actually on the object - rather than the live _dist the readout accumulates, so the board is about the picture and not about how far someone has pushed it. Removal is `layers = 0` on the VisualInstance3D leaves throughout, never visible = false.
dna.declined: `opening` (agreement_gauge's word, seconded by dot_aligner, dot_product_projector and exercise_5_9_angle_between) was the obvious handed-down third use and is refused on TWO independent grounds, either of which is sufficient. First, projection_shadow's test: the pose the word names - the angle between the two vectors whose product this is - is ALREADY the live exported slider. push_angle is 0..1, config-reachable through apply_grid_config, declared in the registry parameters block, and it sweeps exactly theta. A second word for a knob that exists is a fake genome. Second, and worse, the answers do not fit: agreeing/strangers/opposing/parallel are 35, 90, 140 and 0 degrees, and a mower handle at 90 degrees is a pole and at 180 degrees is a mower being pulled backwards by a rope. push_angle spans 16 to 64 degrees because that is the range in which the object is still a lawnmower, so three of the four values would name a machine this one is not. Taking a word without its answers is the dishonest half of a shared vocabulary. ALSO REFUSED: a purchase-style trade of F against d at constant product, which is torque_crank's bargain applied to W = F d. It is real arithmetic and it is unmeasurable here, because _settle normalises the rig to a fixed 2.8 m span - lengthen d and the whole diagram is scaled down to compensate, so two values differ as the same picture at two magnifications. capture_config_sweep's own header calls that the single worst measurement bug this rig has had; there is no reason to buy it deliberately. push_angle and the five colours stay plain exports: a steeper push and a recolour are not arguments.
dna.still_note: framing 0.65, and the reason is a SIBLING NODE. _ensure_lawn deferred-spawns a 6.9 x 5.3 m lawn - a soil slab plus 440 seeded blades - onto get_parent(), which in the sweep is the SubViewport, so it is not measured by _subtree_aabb (a sibling, not a descendant) but it is very much in frame. At framing 1.0 the union box is about (2.81, 1.99, 0.68) with expression's board included, radius 1.76, and PAD 1.9 opens the frame to roughly 6.7 m across - the lawn then fills it wall to wall and every value shares a large constant background, which is dilution. 0.65 narrows the frame to about 4.3 m, putting the machine at roughly 65 percent of frame width. It cannot crop: the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, so 0.65 keeps about 24 percent margin on the furthest corner. The lawn is seeded from hash(seed) ^ 0x5A17 and seed is 0 in every variant, so it is identical in all four frames and adds no noise - only dilution, which is what the framing hint is for. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass and this arithmetic is the evidence offered in its place. If the critic reports faint, check subject share before touching the design: the candidate fault is the lawn, not the axis.

force_mower.name: Force Mower (W = F d cos θ)
force_mower.description: The lawn-mower work diagram turned into a thing you push - an embodied force-display prop for the vectors-forces arc. Push the mower by its angled handle; the push F splits into the part that does work (F cos θ, along the ground) and the part wasted into the dirt (F sin θ, downward). The force vectors live on the object: F down the handle, the horizontal F cos θ, the green dashed vertical decomposition, the long purple displacement d, and a W = F d cos θ readout. DNA: push_angle 0..1 raises the handle angle θ so cos θ - the share of work - shrinks (steeper push, less work done).

parameters.push_angle: 0..1 handle/push angle θ (flat to steep) - cos θ shrinks the work (default 0.45)

dna.default: decomposition=both - `both` is the `_` branch of the match and rebuilds the shipped body of _redraw line for line: the three dashed 0.006 guides walking ZERO -> (fx,0,0) -> (fx,fy,0) -> tip at the same dim 0.6/0.62/0.68 glow, then the three 0.016 component arrows leaving the origin behind the same absf(f) > 0.05 gates, then the 0.03 resultant and the same billboarded readout, added to demo_root in the same order. Nothing else moved: _resting_force, _build_body, _process and the _last_f short-circuit are untouched. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, Vectors_Act5_ForceAsPlace, Void_Crossing) place the bare token `force_cube` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists - and when it IS reached, _last_f is only invalidated if the word is in DECOMPOSITIONS and differs from the current value, so a call naming nothing this artifact owns still rebuilds nothing.
dna.was: seven exports - five colours, a seed and a push - and one hard-coded way of taking a force apart. The three coloured legs left the origin and a dashed staircase walked the same three components tip to tail, both always, welded into the body of _redraw. A map could set how LONG the vector was and what COLOUR it was, never what the object claimed a vector is made of. The runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, and on the question that matters that was true.
dna.note: decomposition is HOW THE COMPONENTS ARE PUT ON THE GEOMETRY, and the word plus the meanings of chain, box and none are taken character for character from basis_vectors_rig (commons_artifacts), vector_magnitude_demo and example_1_5_vector_magnitude_vr, which ask the same question of the same three RGB legs. This is the one member of that family you can PICK UP, which is why the word belongs here: on the other three benches the decomposition is of a vector drawn for you, here it is of a vector you are holding, and the legs re-resolve in the cube's own frame as you turn it. chain walks the legs tip to tail as solid arrows so the last one lands exactly on the resultant's point; box draws the twelve edges of the solid the components span, closed on the tip so the resultant IS its diagonal; none leaves the claim to the arrow and the readout.
dna.kin: The value list is NOT the family's list, and the missing rung is `star` - all three legs leaving the origin, the terms rather than the path. It is absent for a MEASUREMENT reason, not a taxonomic one, exactly as `source` is absent from vector_field_grid's `field`. This artifact already draws the star: `both` IS star plus the walked guide, so `star` would differ from the default by the presence of three dashed cylinders of 6 mm radius and nothing else. Rasterising the four values at the harness's own numbers (RES 760, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, union AABB, four plausible seeded resting directions) puts that pair at 0.12-0.29% of frame against a 2.0% bite threshold: a duplicate tile bought in advance, which is the refusal ftc_bridge made of `axiom` on the same grounds.
dna.still_note: MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, and the number is honest about being marginal. This subject is thin ink - a 0.40 m glass cube plus one 0.03 m resultant, three 0.016 m legs and up to sixty 0.006 m dashes on a 1.24 m vector - so the axis is real in world space and close to the floor of what this bench can see. Rasterising the four values over four plausible resting directions at framing 0.55 gives a peak pairwise change of 2.01-2.58% and a weakest pair (both vs chain) of 0.46-1.46%; at framing 1.0 the same axis peaks at 0.51%. framing 0.55 is the tightest value that still cannot crop, because the rig fits by bounding SPHERE and 0.55 is above 1/PAD = 0.53; the raster agrees, putting the furthest projected point at 325-355 px of the 380 px half-frame. THE ONE THING THAT COULD STILL GO WRONG: _resting_force draws its direction from _rng seeded with hash(seed), and a draw close to a single axis (say 0.95, 0.25, 0.05) leaves almost nothing to decompose - that direction measured 2.01% where a well-spread one measured 2.58%. If the sweep returns faint, change `seed` before believing anything about the design. No fixture is needed otherwise: the cube is frozen with zero velocity, so _process takes the resting-vector branch and the still is already reproducible.
dna.declines: `rest` - what the cube claims when no hand is on it - was designed, measured and refused. _resting_force invents a seeded arbitrary vector for an object nobody is touching, and sample|weight|normal|zero is a genuine argument about that. It is not shipped for two reasons, both hard. A vertical weight or normal has ONE nonzero component, so at two of its four values the decomposition axis has nothing to draw and the cross sweep would publish identical tiles under different words - the same fault refused above, bought twice. And `rest` is the axis a player destroys by picking the cube up, which is the one thing this artifact is for; decomposition is the axis that survives the hand. push and seed stay plain exports: a longer arrow is a bigger photograph of the same claim. The five colours stay plain exports; a recolour is not an argument.

force_cube.name: Force Cube (a vector you hold)
force_cube.description: A grabbable cube that draws the force you apply as an arrow out of its centre, split into x / y / z components - an embodied force-display prop. The cube IS the tail of the vector: wherever you push it the arrow points, and the three coloured component arrows (red Fx, green Fy, blue Fz) plus a dashed decomposition box show how one push is really three. A faint motion trail follows. DNA: push 0..1 is the force magnitude; seed sets its direction (live, both come from the grabbing hand's motion).

dna.default: workings=trace - trace is the fall-through arm of the match and runs no code at all, and the whole match sits AFTER _settle(rig, 1.9), so the legacy fit and placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. Two edits above that line: three nodes bound to locals that were previously passed straight into add_child, and the four dashed cone edges wrapped in an identity Node3D named SpreadCone so the axis can reach the whole envelope in one call. pickable_prop._subtree_aabb recurses into Node3D children and does NOT apply their transform, and this holder is never moved, so the settled box is bit-identical. The gun, the reservoir, the trigger, the seeded bubble pool and _process are untouched. All 3 placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, MindMap_VectorForces, Vectors_Act3_FieldsAndMotion) carry the bare token `bubble_blaster` or `bubble_blaster:0:0` with no config key at all, so the new branch in apply_grid_config is unreachable from every map that exists.
dna.was: no axis at all - the runner refused this token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. seed, output and four colours are @exports that lengthen, widen or recolour ONE fixed claim: a single mean arrow down the muzzle axis and four dashed edges sketching where the spray stops. The artifact's own truth line says every emitter is a little vector field made of thousands of tiny departures, and the object had exactly one way of drawing that - as one arrow, the average of a thing it was arguing is not one.
dna.shared_with: transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded by its own bench-mates dot_aligner, vector_add, vector_sub, projection_shadow, launch_arc, torque_crank and bounce_well. A launch velocity is a scalar times a direction, which is the same product those benches take apart. DERIVED from the @export_enum in bubble_blaster.gd, not transcribed.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. WHAT IT SHOWS STANDING STILL, checked first because firing needs a hand the bench does not have: _build calls _place_bubbles(), which distributes the whole pool across phases 0..1 along the cone, so the still already shows a full spreading cone of bubbles at _fire_level 0 - dim rather than glowing, and drifting at a tenth speed. Nothing about this axis depends on the trigger. OPERANDS is the value that carries the argument: the averaged arrow and the dashed envelope go dark and thirteen departure vectors are drawn from the nozzle instead, all of the same LENGTH (the speed is the scalar) along a golden-angle spiral through the cone disc (the spread is the direction), with the half-angle swept as an arc against a thin axis ray. The spiral is arithmetic, not randomness - no RNG is touched, so the bundle is the same bundle in every frame. OUTCOME is the picture of this machine NOT doing the one thing it exists to do: arrow, envelope and readout unlayered, leaving a gun and some soap, which is what every other bubble machine looks like. EXPRESSION promotes v_i = v_out . d_hat_i onto a plate with the live numbers substituted.
dna.declined: `foresight` (catapult's word, seconded by force_pad and human_catapult) was handed over as the promising reading and is refused on two grounds. The value list is parabola|apex|landing|none, and this thing has no parabola: the bubbles leave in straight lines inside a cone, under no gravity, and recycle at the far end. There is no apex and there is no landing, so three of the four answers name a mechanism this object lacks - folding_past's refusal, exactly. And the premise fails too: foresight is how much of the flight you are given BEFORE you fire, which requires a before. This gun wears its launch vector on the muzzle whether or not anyone is holding it, so there is no state in which the vector is a prediction rather than a label. launch_arc refused the same word for the mirror-image reason - its arc is a completed flight rather than a preview - and the two refusals together are the shape of the word: it belongs to machines that fire ONE thing and can show you where it will land. ALSO REFUSED, and this one was measured rather than reasoned: `field`, the shape of the launch distribution (solid cone, hollow shell, parallel beam, flat fan). It is a genuine argument, it is this artifact's own, and `output` cannot reach it - spread is clamped to 7..28 degrees and never zero. It is not shipped because it is INVISIBLE TO A STILL AT THIS SCALE. The 11 to 26 bubbles have radii 0.020-0.055 m and _settle scales the rig by about 0.888; at framing 0.60 the frame is roughly 2.9 m across at 760 px, so the entire bubble pool covers on the order of 0.4 percent of frame. Moving all of it would sit an order of magnitude under the bite threshold, which is the 'axis real in world space, invisible in frame' row of the brief's table bought in advance. output and seed stay plain exports; a longer arrow is a bigger photograph of the same claim.
dna.still_note: framing 0.60, derived rather than guessed, and honest about being the tight end. The union box with expression's board is roughly (1.90, 1.44, 0.75) after _settle, radius about 1.25, and the no-crop floor is 1/PAD = 0.526, so 0.60 leaves about 14 percent margin on the furthest corner. It is needed because the ink this axis moves is THIN: the launch arrow is about 1.37 m long and 0.05 m wide and the four dashed edges are 0.012 m wide, which is on the order of 1 percent of frame at framing 1.0. They are also the BRIGHTEST pixels in the frame - glow energy 1.8 on the arrow against a matte pink body - so the focus number (hottest 5 percent) should move far more than the frame number, and operands should be the strongest value because it replaces one arrow with thirteen. ONE RESIDUAL RISK, named rather than hidden: _process advances _stream_t by delta * 0.10 while idle, so the bubble pool drifts a little during the 1.1 s settle and the exact bubble positions depend on frame timing rather than on the axis. The bubbles are small and identical across values, so this is noise and not bias, but it is the reason a sub-1 percent verdict on this artifact should be read as a capture fact before it is read as a design fact. NOT MEASURED - no capture was run in this pass.

bubble_blaster.name: Bubble Blaster (output velocity vector)
bubble_blaster.description: A soap-bubble gun that fires a spreading cone of bubbles and wears its launch vector on the muzzle - an embodied force-display prop. Pull the trigger and bubbles pour out; the muzzle shows an arrow for the output velocity and a faint cone for the spread. Crank the output and the arrow stretches, the cone widens, the bubbles fly faster and further. Every emitter is a little vector field - each particle leaves with a velocity, and the spray's force is just that launch vector made of many departures. DNA: output 0..1 dials the launch (vector length, spread angle, bubble speed/count); seed jitters the bubbles.

parameters.output: 0..1 launch output - vector length, spread, bubble count (default 0.6)

vector_add.name: Vector Addition (a + b, two-pad console)
vector_add.description: Vector addition made playable - the entry operation of the embodied vectors-forces arc, a ToyConsole with a TWO-PAD control surface (synthesised from three interaction-design passes). Two 2D pads on the front lip, one per vector: drag a pad and that vector's tip follows your hand (a grabbed handle in VR, a pointer-drag on desktop). The two arrows draw head-to-tail on the console top and the resultant a+b swings live; the monitor shows the full component breakdown (a, b, a+b, |a+b|, angle). The control IS the vector tip. seed sets the starting a and b.

parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)

vector_sub.name: Vector Subtraction (a − b, two-pad console)
vector_sub.description: Vector subtraction made playable - the same two-pad ToyConsole as vector_add, flipped to a - b = a + (-b). Two 2D pads place the tips of a and b; the demo draws a, then the negated b head-to-tail, and the resultant a-b, with a faint ghost of the original +b so the flip reads as the whole idea. The monitor shows a, b, a-b, |a-b| and the angle. The control IS the vector tip; seed sets the starting a and b.

parameters.op: forced to sub by the scene
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)

orbit_pair.name: Orbit Pair (gravity, F = G m₁m₂/r²)
orbit_pair.description: Gravity and orbits made playable - the clean rebuild of the old two-body sim, for the embodied vectors-forces arc. Two bodies pull on each other along the line between them, equal and opposite (Newton's third law), and orbit their shared centre of mass (the barycenter). Make one heavier and the barycenter slides toward it while the orbits resize - an equal binary becomes a star with a far-flung planet. Shows the two bodies on their dotted orbits, the equal-and-opposite gravity vectors, velocity tangents, the barycenter and the line of attraction, with an F = G m1m2/r^2 readout. DNA: mass_ratio 0..1 from a symmetric binary to a dominant star+planet; seed sets the orbital phase; color_a star, color_b planet, accent gravity vectors, orbit_color the paths.

parameters.mass_ratio: 0..1 from equal binary to dominant star+planet - shifts the barycenter and resizes the orbits (default 0.6)

circle_train.name: Circle Train (centripetal force, a = v²/r)
circle_train.description: Centripetal force made playable - a sci-fi intermezzo for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A high-speed neon maglev loop: the train's velocity is always tangent to the ring (grows with v) and its force always points inward toward the centre (grows with v^2/r). The payoff you can dial: double the speed and the inward force quadruples - the velocity arrow stretches linearly while the centripetal force arrow explodes. Glowing torus track, a banking train of cars, speed streaks, the tangent + inward vectors, and a v / a / F_c readout. DNA: speed 0..1 dials the train (velocity ~v linear, centripetal force ~v^2 quadratic); seed sets the train position; color_a neon track, color_b velocity, accent centripetal force, train_color the cars.

parameters.speed: 0..1 train speed - velocity grows linearly, centripetal force quadratically (default 0.7)
parameters.turn: standard | wide | tight - the r in a = v^2/r, how tight the curve is (default standard)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)

dna.default: turn=standard, workings=trace - standard SHORT-CIRCUITS: _track_radius() never enters the match and hands back the shipped const TRACK_R = 1.0 itself, rather than re-deriving 1.0 from a table, so every expression that used to read TRACK_R reads the same float from the same source. trace is the fall-through arm of a match that sits AFTER _settle(rig) and runs no code at all. Nothing above that line changed except two identity Node3D holders (Train, Streaks) that hold the cars and the streak spheres at their own absolute rig-local positions - _subtree_aabb recurses into Node3D children, so the settle box, the scale and the mount placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. All 3 existing placements (Force_Props_Sandbox, VFM_05_Launch, VFM_Forces_Playground) carry the bare token circle_train with no config overrides, so apply_grid_config never sees either key
dna.was: seven @exports - a seed, a 0..1 speed, a complexity and four colours. Only speed touches the physics, and the runner refused the artifact for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The deeper weld is that a = v^2/r has TWO symbols and the bench could only ever dial one of them: r was a const, so the exhibit could not make the claim its own description makes about the radius. What the bench draws of the force was equally fixed - the train, the streaks and both arrows, always, with no way to strip the spectacle off the vector or to state the perpendicularity in the picture instead of the caption
dna.shared_with: workings is transform_composition_workbench's word with its four values in the same order, seconded on this bench by dot_aligner, projection_shadow, torque_crank, bounce_well and launch_arc; DERIVED from the @export_enum in circle_train.gd, not transcribed. turn is this artifact's own word: torque_crank's `purchase` (balanced|long|stub) is the same SHAPE of axis over the same symbol r, but purchase means leverage - how much moment a given force buys - and a turn radius buys nothing. Taking that word would have imported an answer this object does not give
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05. turn is measurable BECAUSE of _settle(): the ToyConsole rescales the demo rig to a fixed 0.78 m span, so all three rings are photographed at the same width and what changes in the frame is the RATIO of the inward arrow to the circle it bends. At the shipped speed 0.7 (v = 1.185) the arrow is 0.59 long against radius 1.00 on standard, 0.35 against 1.80 on wide, and 1.07 against 0.55 on tight - where the pull is nearly twice the radius, runs through the hub and out the far side. That is v^2/r drawn instead of asserted. The code was already written as if r varied: car_gap = 0.34 / TRACK_R holds the coupling ARC-LENGTH constant so the cars stay the same size on any ring, which is the tell that the const was a parameter nobody had named. workings=operands is the value that carries the artifact's actual claim - a still cannot show that the force turns the train, but it can show that the force is PERPENDICULAR to the motion, so operands extends the tangent forward and back through the train as the straight line it would otherwise take and plants a right-angle gnomon between that line and the inward arrow. The axes are independent: turn sets the geometry, workings decides how it is annotated, and a tight ring is still a tight ring at workings=expression

launch_arc.name: Launch Arc (projectile motion)
launch_arc.description: Projectile motion made playable - the launch / F=ma toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc (the pad that throws you). A launch pad fires at angle theta with speed v; gravity bends the straight launch vector into a parabola. The launch velocity decomposes into a horizontal vx (carries you) and a vertical vy (fights gravity); the trade between them sets the range = v^2 sin(2theta)/g - which peaks at 45 degrees. Shows the tilted glowing pad, the stroboscopic projectile arc, the launch vector + its vx/vy components, and apex / range markers. DNA: angle 0..1 sets the launch angle (flat to steep), power 0..1 the launch speed; color_a pad + components, color_b the arc + launch vector, accent pad glow + apex/range.

parameters.angle: 0..1 launch angle, flat to steep - range peaks at 45 deg (default 0.5)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)
parameters.comparison: single | fan | pairs | envelope - what the one throw is shown against, every companion fired at the same v0 (default single)

dna.default: workings=trace, comparison=single - both are the fall-through arm of their own match and run no code whatever, and both matches sit AFTER _settle(rig). Nothing above that line was touched by this pass: the tilted pad, the base plate, the ground bar, the stroboscopic parabola, the launch vector, the dashed vx/vy legs and the apex/range/drop markers are the same calls with the same literals in the same order, so the fit, the scale and the placement are computed from exactly the geometry that shipped. drag_lane.name: Drag Lane (F = -b·v you feel)
drag_lane.description: Friction / drag made felt - a forces toy for the embodied vectors-forces arc. A runner enters a resistant medium at full tilt and slows under F = -b*v, so its velocity decays v ~ e^(-bt). Frozen stroboscopically, the runner's snapshots bunch together and its velocity arrows shrink as the drag eats the motion - run through air, water, honey and each pulls back harder. DNA: drag 0..1 sweeps from glide (snapshots evenly spread) to dead-stop (piled up fast); seed jitters the medium motes; color_a lane, color_b runner + velocity, accent drag particles, medium_color the resistant volume.

parameters.drag: 0..1 drag strength - sweeps the velocity decay from glide to dead-stop (default 0.5)

projection_shadow.name: Projection Shadow ((a·n̂)n̂ as a shadow)
projection_shadow.description: Vector projection made playable - the third operations toy with dot_aligner (dot) and torque_crank (cross). A sun overhead, an object floating off a rail; the object's shadow lands on the rail, and the shadow's distance from the origin IS a*n_hat - the projection of the object's position onto the axis n_hat. The perpendicular drop from object to shadow is the rejection (what doesn't live along n_hat). DNA: projection 0..1 swings the object from perpendicular (a perp n, no shadow) to along the rail (a parallel n, full shadow); seed jitters length; color_a rail/axis, color_b the vector a, accent the projection shadow, sun_color the light.

parameters.projection: 0..1 swings the object from perpendicular to along the rail - drives a*n_hat and the shadow length (default 0.7)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)

torque_crank.name: Torque Crank (r × F you can feel)
torque_crank.description: The cross product made playable - the operations pair to dot_aligner. A lever arm r and a push F meet at the hub of a flywheel; the torque tau = r x F = |r||F|sin(theta) points up the axle and spins the wheel. Force along the arm does nothing (sin 0); force across it spins hardest (sin 90). Shows r (cyan), F (orange), the tau torque axis (gold, up the axle), spin arrows and an rpm readout. DNA: leverage 0..1 sets the angle between r and F (0 = along the arm, 1 = perpendicular); seed jitters the arm bearing; color_a steel rig, color_b arm, force_color push, accent torque axis + flywheel glow.

parameters.leverage: 0..1 angle of the push F from the arm r - drives the torque sin(theta), the tau vector length and the spin (default 0.78)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default trace)
parameters.purchase: balanced | long | stub - how the same torque is bought, |r| against |F| at a constant product (default balanced)
parameters.accent: The torque axis tau + flywheel glow

Every derived quantity is therefore unchanged by construction: torque_mag is still clampf(r_dir.cross(f_dir).length()), the tau length is still 0.25 + torque_mag * 0.85, the wheel still turns torque_mag * 48 degrees and the monitor still reads the same rpm. dot_aligner.name: Dot-Aligner (aim · foe = mercy)
dot_aligner.description: The dot product made playable, and the embodied vectors-forces arc's operations toy. A swivel turret on a pedestal aims at a drifting foe-cube; the gold AIM vector (a) and the cyan DIRECTION-TO-FOE vector (b) meet at an angle, and a*b = cos(theta) is the charge. As alignment rises the angle closes, a lock BEAM ignites, and the foe converts FOE -> FRIEND (red -> green) - agreement here is mercy, not a kill. DNA: alignment 0..1 sets how locked the aim is (drives cos(theta), the beam, the conversion); seed jitters the foe bearing; color_a steel rig, color_b vectors, accent lock beam, foe_color/friend_color the conversion.

parameters.alignment: 0..1 how closely the aim points at the foe - drives cos(theta), the beam, and the conversion (default 0.78)
parameters.opening: agreeing | strangers | opposing | parallel - the case the pair is found in, i.e. the angle a and b meet at (default agreeing)
parameters.workings: outcome | trace | operands | expression - how much of the arithmetic the bench draws (default operands)

Checked numerically at alignment 0.00 / 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.78 / 1.00: bit-identical to the shipped expression at every position. The readout gains its case line only when opening is NOT agreeing, so the monitor string is byte-identical too. operands is the fall-through arm of the workings match and adds nothing. All 5 existing placements (MindMap_VectorForces, Force_Props_Sandbox, VFM_02_Operations, VFM_Operations_Playground, Vectors_Act2_VectorArithmetic) carry the bare token dot_aligner:0:0 with no config overrides, so they run on both defaults and are unchanged

The turret could only ever be found broadly agreeing and made to agree harder - the three cases the dot product exists to teach (the dot vanishing, the dot going negative, the dot at its ceiling) were unreachable from a map token AND from the player's hand

dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-05 - the runner refused it for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. ASKED THE GEOMETRY RATHER THAN ASSUMING: a rotation about UP is not the angle between the vectors, because b keeps a vertical component (dir_to_foe.y is 0.177 after normalising) that the spin never touches, so a rotation of phi leaves an angle of acos(y*y + (1-y*y)*cos phi). Rotating by a flat 90 degrees would have left cos(theta) = 0.031 and 'strangers' would have been a near-miss wearing an exact name; _miss_rotation() solves for the phi that makes each claim true instead. Measured: agreeing cos 0.963 / theta 15.6 (beam lit, foe warming green), strangers cos 0.0000 exactly / theta 90.0 (beam dead, foe full enemy-red, arc a right angle), opposing cos -0.766 / theta 140.0 (aim swung past the turret's own shoulder), parallel cos 1.0 / theta 0 (arrows superimpose, _add_arc returns early on a zero cross so the arc collapses to nothing, foe CONVERTS to green with the beam at full width). The slider stays live under all four: opening sets the case the turret is found in at the shipped rest and alignment shifts it by the same 72-degree span it has always driven
dna.gotcha: opening MOVES the two arrows and workings REMOVES them (outcome unlayers both plus the arc). The two axes therefore disturb the same brightest pixels by different means - opening should read as a large focus bite and outcome as a large frame bite, and if they score the same way something is wrong with the capture, not the design

combined_forces_demo.name: Combined Forces Demo
combined_forces_demo.description: Vector addition as force combination — multiple forces acting on a body, visualized as arrows that add head-to-tail. The resultant force emerges from superposition. Use #composition: and #force_count:.

That is this bench, and the geometry was measured rather than assumed. The ball hangs at the CENTRE of a 1x1x1 containment (SCENE_SCALE 0.33, so 0.33 m in world). r = (0.15,0,0) and F = (0,2,0), so tau = r x F = (0,0,0.30) and the arrow, drawn at tau*0.5, reaches 0.0495 m along +Z from the ball; -tau reaches the same 0.0495 m along -Z. Both stand in open air. The artifact could not be photographed being wrong, and a claim that cannot fail is not visibly true either.
dna.note: lever is WHETHER THE LAW BINDS, not which law. solved is Calder's arithmetic, pivot placed so w_l*d_l = w_r*d_r and every rod dead level. halved cuts each rod in the middle - symmetry mistaken for balance, the mistake anyone makes who has not done the sum. inverted applies the law with the ratio reversed, the heavier child on the LONGER arm. The residual moment is not styled: the rod is hung by it, at asin(residual / (arm*W)), and the ladder falls out of the algebra rather than being chosen - halved leaves arm*(wr-wl)/2 and inverted leaves arm*(wr-wl), so the sign error leaves exactly twice the residual of the naive cut, in the same direction; sin(theta) doubles exactly and the angle a little more than doubles, since asin is convex. ONE HONEST PROXY, stated plainly so nobody mistakes it for physics: a rod whose loads hang on free wires carries cos(theta) in every moment term, so its only equilibrium is vertical with the heavy end straight down, and the true free-swing answer would fold the sculpture into a tangle at every non-default value. What is drawn is the residual normalised by the largest moment the arm could carry - zero exactly when the law is obeyed, which is why solved is untouched.
dna.kin: evidence is the family word taken character for character from the 34 siblings, THREE VALUES not four. There is no axiom tier because the plaque already IS the symbolic assertion - tau = w*d is printed on it at longhand - so a fourth value would be the third one minus its numbers, which is trace read backwards. The default is longhand rather than the motion demos' result, for weather_vector_field's stated reason: this artifact was born with its whole working on the table, a gram tag under every disc and a total on the plaque. NOT named `law`, although force_field_visualizer declares an axis by that word: over there the four values are four different force laws falling off differently, here there is one law and the question is whether it is solved, ignored or inverted. NOT `balance` either - that names the state, and lever names the mechanism that produces it.
dna.still_note: lever is the silhouette axis and should bite hard: every rod above the leaves rotates, so each disc moves in x AND y and the whole tree goes lopsided; inverted should measure at AT LEAST twice halved's displacement, in the same direction, so the two are ORDERED and not merely different - a pair that comes back unordered is a bug in the tilt, not a soft axis. evidence is the thin one: it removes a handful of Label3D gram tags and a four-line plaque from a 3.6 m sculpture, so expect dilution and crop-recheck before believing INERT. One coupling to know about: the plaque's own text changes with lever (balanced -> NOT balanced), so a diff along evidence at a non-default lever is not measuring evidence alone. Judge evidence at lever=solved.
dna.declines: use_objects stays a plain export and is deliberately NOT an axis: the corpus already ships that value as a separate token, calder_object_mobile.tscn, which sets use_objects=true, seed=13, depth=3 and has its own registry entry and its own placement in Sky_Climb. Declaring it here would sweep a family whose second member already has a name. seed, depth, span, leaf_prob and top_y stay dials - a different random tree is a different object, not a different argument.

calder_mobile.name: Calder Mobile (balanced, real weights)
calder_mobile.description: A large hanging Calder mobile that is actually balanced. Every arm obeys the lever law τ = w·d: the two children of each rod are weighed, then the pivot is placed so w_left·d_left = w_right·d_right - the heavier shape rides the shorter arm - and the whole thing hangs level from a single ceiling point. Leaf masses are real: each flat painted disc is sheet aluminium, mass = π r²·t·ρ (t = 3 mm, ρ = 2700 kg/m³). Calder's primaries - red, yellow, blue, black, white. A plaque states the real total mass and the balance principle. Improves on the project's earlier calder_mobile_primaries, which was only a palette totem, not a balanced mobile.
calder_mobile.qfep_connection: A hanging Calder mobile that actually balances — every arm obeying the lever law, torque answering torque all the way up the tree. The chapter of forces made into sculpture that hangs in equilibrium: not a picture of balance but balance itself, each branch a solved equation, the whole a mobile that would tip if a single mass were wrong.

dna.default: lever=solved, evidence=longhand - the export defaults, untouched by this scene. calder_object_mobile.tscn sets use_objects=true, seed=13 and depth=3 and says nothing about either axis, so its one placement (Sky_Climb) builds the identical tree from the identical _rng draw order it always did.
dna.was: not a separate artifact at all - the same CalderMobile script under a second .tscn, which is this corpus's most common hidden family. Before this pass neither name could turn anything.
dna.note: declared here as well as on calder_mobile because they are ONE SCRIPT under TWO scene files, and an axis declared on only one of the pair is an axis half the maps cannot reach. The values are not copied - they are the same code, so the two tokens must measure ALIKE, and a sweep that says otherwise is reporting a fixture difference (use_objects=true, depth=3 here) rather than a difference of axis. See calder_mobile for the full note; the only thing that differs is what hangs on the arms, discs there and project primitives here, and that difference is already the reason these two names exist.
dna.still_note: depth=3 here against 4 on the sibling, so there are fewer arms and each tilt at halved/inverted is a larger share of a smaller tree. The leaf masses are the OBJECTS table (0.18 / 0.55 / 0.42 / 0.7 kg) rather than continuous disc areas, so the residual moments come in coarser steps and two arms can tilt identically - that is the mass table, not a dead axis.

Each primitive carries a plausible mass and the arms balance those masses by the lever law, so the foundational shapes of the curriculum drift in equilibrium. A plaque states the total mass. Same CalderMobile script with use_objects = true.

pendulum_hall.name: Pendulum Hall (walk-in)

The restoring force mg sin θ hauls the bob back through bottom-dead-centre; a glowing arc on the floor records the swept path; the weight / tension / restoring vectors ride the bob at the scale of your own body. Stand in the hall and watch the giant bob pass. The large half of the 'intimate toy -> walk-in installation' pair (clusters with pendulum_swing).

centrifuge_ring.name: Centrifuge Ring (walk-in centripetal)
centrifuge_ring.description: The body-scale, walk-in twin of circle_train: a pod laps a big neon ring while the velocity (tangent) and centripetal force (inward, ∝ v²/r) ride it at your own scale. Velocity is always tangent, the force always toward the centre you never reach; crank the speed and the inward arrow explodes as the square. a = v²/r made into a ridden loop you stand inside.

spring_tower.name: Spring Tower (walk-in Hooke)

orbit_walk.name: Orbit Walk (walk-in two-body)

Make one heavier and the barycenter slides toward it, the orbits resizing to keep the balance. An orbit is two things falling toward each other and missing, around a centre that belongs to neither.

drag_corridor.name: Drag Corridor (walk-in air/water/honey)

A probe in each zone glides and dies under F = -b*v, its velocity arrow shrinking as it bunches up — the same launch goes far in air, less in water, barely a lunge in honey. Drag is the world charging you rent on speed.

work_meter.name: Work Meter (W = F·d·cosθ)
work_meter.description: The intimate companion to force_mower for Work: a block on a rail and a force applied at an angle theta, so only the along-the-ground part (F cos theta, green) does work while the perpendicular part (F sin theta) is wasted. Raise the angle and the work falls even though you push just as hard. The world only feels the part of a force that goes its way.

free_vector.name: Free Vector (direction + length)
free_vector.description: The intimate companion to VectorBasics for Vector basics: one arrow and its ghost copies, carried to different origins to show a vector has no home. A vector is two facts only - a direction and a length; slide it anywhere and it is the same vector. A vector is a journey with no starting address.

coordinate_locator.name: Coordinate Locator (applied coordinates)
coordinate_locator.description: Applied coordinate system: a beacon locates a real point by reading off its (x, y, z) address, dropping dashed lines to each axis the way GPS pins you to the grid. Space is a promise three numbers keep.

route_vector.name: Route Vector (applied displacement)
route_vector.description: Applied vector basics: a from-pin and a to-pin, and the one arrow between them is the displacement - the trip, not the places. A courier walks the arrow. A vector is a journey with no starting address.

river_crossing.name: River Crossing (applied subtraction)

brake_skid.name: Brake Skid (applied friction)

magnitude_bench.name: Magnitude Bench (|v| = sqrt(x2+y2+z2))

torque_bench.name: Torque Bench (tau = |r||F| sin th)
torque_bench.description: Bench-scale torque: a lever on a pivot and a force at its end; push along the arm and nothing turns, push across it and it spins hardest. Only the perpendicular part makes torque. tau = |r||F| sin theta.

centripetal_bench.name: Centripetal Bench (a = v2/r)
centripetal_bench.description: Bench-scale centripetal: a tabletop turntable, a mass circling a hub, velocity tangent and force inward. a = v2/r - the inward arrow is the only thing bending the straight line into a circle.

restitution_bench.name: Restitution Bench (h' = e h)
restitution_bench.description: Bench-scale restitution: a strobe of one ball's bounces, each peak a fixed fraction of the last, with a live ball hopping through them. h' = e*h - the coefficient of restitution is the tax on every fall.

newton_bench.name: Newton Bench (F = m a)
newton_bench.description: Bench-scale Newton's second law: a mass on a table, a force pushing it, the acceleration it produces. a = F/m, dialed live. The cleanest statement of what a force does.

velocity_bench.name: Velocity Bench (v = vx + vy)
velocity_bench.description: Bench-scale velocity: a puck crossing a table with its velocity drawn and split into the part that carries it across (vx) and the part that lifts it (vy). Motion is a vector the world keeps editing.

wind_toy.name: Wind Toy (held vane)
wind_toy.description: The small, held end of Wind: a pinwheel on a stick and a streamer that leans - the least you need to feel a force you cannot see. wind_bench.name: Wind Bench (fan + windsock)
wind_bench.description: The bench-scale middle of Wind: a desk fan and a windsock, the push made readable as the sock swings from hanging to horizontal. F = half rho v squared Cd A grows with the square of speed. Wind is air with somewhere to be; the force is in the speed, squared.

wind_room.name: Wind Room (walk-in field)
wind_room.description: The room-scale, walk-in end of Wind: a field of tall windsocks you stand among, all leaning the same way, so the invisible field becomes a place. A wind field is one direction and one speed filling the space. Wind is a force that has decided to be everywhere at once - and you are in it.

work_toy.name: Work Toy (held W = F.d.cos th)
work_toy.description: Hand-scale Work: a small block pushed a short distance at an angle; the useful along-the-ground part does work, the perpendicular part is wasted. The world only feels the part of a force that goes its way.

work_room.name: Work Room (walk-in F.d)

lever_toy.name: Lever Toy (held seesaw)

lever_room.name: Lever Room (walk-in balance beam)

vector_bench.name: Vector Bench (direction + length)
vector_bench.description: Bench-scale vector basics: an arrow that sweeps both its direction and its length, with its components drawn. A vector is two facts only - a direction and a length.

scaling_bench.name: Scaling Bench (k x v)

field_bench.name: Field Bench (a vector at every point)

magnitude_hall.name: Magnitude Hall (walk-in |v|)

force_room.name: Force Room (walk-in F = m.a)

projection_toy.name: Projection Toy (held, onto a line)
projection_toy.description: Hand-scale projection: a vector and a rail; the shadow of the vector along the rail is the projection (v.n_hat), the perpendicular drop is the rejection. Projection is the part of you that lives along someone else's line.
